tagline: For a secure, affordable and sustainable energy future.
hero_kpi_rationale: Marked recovery in operating margin (+6.3 pts) reflecting the rebound in oil prices and cost reductions following a very difficult 2015.

kpis.name: Gross Margin
kpis.explanation: The portion of revenue that remains after paying direct production costs.
kpis.description: Gross margin improved slightly in 2016, driven by cost optimization in refining operations.
kpis.signal: Stability despite a volatile energy environment

kpis.name: Operating Margin
kpis.explanation: Profit generated from core operations before taxes, expressed as a percentage of revenue.
kpis.description: Operating margin increased significantly due to the recovery in oil prices and cost reductions.
kpis.signal: Strong rebound following a heavily impacted 2015

kpis.name: Capital Expenditures
kpis.explanation: Spending on building or acquiring productive facilities.
kpis.description: BP maintains a disciplined capex policy to strengthen financial resilience after a challenging period.
kpis.signal: Significant reduction in capex amid financial discipline

kpis.name: Total Headcount
kpis.description: BP reduced headcount to 74,500 employees to adapt to a leaner model following the oil crisis.
kpis.signal: Workforce reduction as part of a restructuring plan

kpis.name: R&D Investment (% of Revenue)
kpis.explanation: Portion of revenue allocated to research and development.
kpis.description: BP allocates a marginal share of its revenue to R&D, typical for an integrated energy company.
kpis.signal: Very low R&D compared to tech standards, normal for an energy company

kpis.name: Hydrocarbon Production
kpis.explanation: Total daily volume of crude oil and natural gas produced.
kpis.description: BP produced 3.3 million barrels of oil equivalent per day in 2016, up 3% from 2015, driven by the start-up of new projects.
kpis.signal: Slight production increase despite low-price environment

kpis.name: Proved Reserves Replacement Ratio
kpis.explanation: Ratio of reserves discovered to reserves produced during the year, expressed as a percentage.
kpis.description: BP replaced 109% of its proved reserves production in 2016, including the impact of the Abu Dhabi onshore concession renewal.
kpis.signal: Excellent reserves replacement ratio above 100%, including renewal of key concessions

kpis.name: Dividend per Share
kpis.description: Annual dividend per share paid, aggregated from yfinance.dividends over the last seven fiscal years reported by the company.
kpis.signal: Dividend per share of 12.3868 GBp in the latest year.

kpis.name: Capital Returned (Dividends)
kpis.description: Capital returned to shareholders via annual dividends, extracted from yfinance.cashflow over the last four fiscal years reported.
kpis.signal: Capital returned to shareholders via dividends of 5.059 Bn GBp in the latest year.

kpis.name: Payout Ratio
kpis.description: Payout Ratio = Dividends Paid / Net Income, calculated over the last three fiscal years from yfinance.cashflow and yfinance.income_stmt.
kpis.signal: Share of net income distributed as dividends: 9198.2% in the latest year.

risks.title: Persistent provisions related to the Gulf of America oil spill
risks.score_rationale: Provisions and liabilities related to the Gulf of America spill amounted to USD 6.938 billion as of March 31, 2026, with explicit uncertainty regarding the final amount and payment timing. The language used ('amounts ultimately payable may differ', 'timing of payments is uncertain') indicates significant and uncapped residual exposure.

risks.title: Sector-specific tax pressure from the UK Energy Profits Levy
risks.score_rationale: The Energy Profits Levy (EPL) raises the effective tax rate on North Sea profits to 78%, an exceptionally high level. The extension of the EPL to March 31, 2030 was substantially adopted in Q1 2025, with material impacts on deferred tax assets reassessed in Q1 2026, signaling a sustained adverse regulatory trend.

risks.title: Hydrocarbon realizations volatility and exposure to market prices
risks.score_rationale: Average realizations on liquids ranged from $51.20/bbl (US) to $85.35/bbl (Europe) in Q1 2026, with significant quarter-on-quarter fluctuations (e.g., natural gas Europe: $8.76/mcf in Q1 2026 vs $16.47/mcf in Q1 2025). This dispersion illustrates a structural dependence on commodity spot prices, central to BP's business model.

risks.title: Rising environmental costs and provisions
risks.score_rationale: Variable environmental costs reached USD 2.399 billion in Q1 2026, up 79% from Q1 2025 (USD 1.337 Bn). Environmental provisions represent a recurring adjustment item (USD 173 M in Q1 2026), signaling increasing regulatory obligations and operational environmental liabilities.

risks.title: Ongoing operational restructuring and rationalization
risks.score_rationale: Restructuring, integration and rationalization costs amounted to USD 249 M in Q1 2026 and USD 344 M in Q1 2025, absent in Q4 2025, indicating an active but irregular transformation program. These recurring charges signal execution risks related to portfolio and workforce reorganization.

risks.title: Accounting complexity of physical commodity contracts treated as derivatives
risks.score_rationale: BP details the fair value accounting effects from IFRS treatment of physical contracts (LNG, pipelines, storage) as derivatives, generating recurring and significant valuation differences between underlying economic performance and reported IFRS results. This representation risk affects result transparency for investors.

risks.title: High leverage and pressure on deleveraging in a low-price environment
risks.score_rationale: Net debt reached USD 25.3 Bn (USD 38.6 Bn including leases) in Q1 2026, with a gearing ratio of 33.4% including leases. Net debt increased by USD 3.1 Bn in one quarter, amid falling Brent prices at USD 81/bbl, signaling pressure on deleveraging capacity and the share buyback program.

risks.title: Energy transition and low-carbon portfolio repositioning
risks.score_rationale: The divestment of onshore wind activities (December 2025) and continued focus on solar, offshore wind, hydrogen and CCS illustrate an ongoing strategic repositioning. The lack of demonstrated profitability in these segments creates reputational and execution risks relative to BP's public climate commitments.

ai_positioning.summary: BP does not mention any strategy or initiative related to artificial intelligence in the 20-F 2016 document. The company does not position AI as a strategic lever.
evidence: No mention of AI, machine learning or advanced algorithms in the report
No reference to tech AI partnerships or acquisitions
Absence of KPIs or projects related to intelligent automation
